target_customer: Companies and IT or AV teams that run conference rooms with existing projectors or TVs
problem: Presenting from a laptop in a meeting room needs cables, adapters and often help from IT. Ubiq lets any device project wirelessly to an existing display.
business_model: Hardware unit plus B2B SaaS subscription for room management and calendar display
product_category: Wireless presentation and meeting room display

founders.name: Sumit Pasupalak
founders.background_notes: Named on the YC page. Background and education not found in an opened source.

founders.name: Jayanth Kottapalli
founders.background_notes: Named on the YC page. Background and education not found in an opened source.

competitors.name: Mersive Solstice
competitors.what: Solstice Pod, a turnkey wireless media streaming box for meeting rooms and classrooms

technical_complexity.rationale: A small team had to ship a hardware hub plus clients that stream secure screen content from any laptop, with a cloud dashboard and calendar integration. Standard engineering with some hard parts around networking and device support.

defensibility.rationale: Several wireless presentation products already existed and the software was copyable. Installed units give mild switching costs.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Established AV vendors already sold wireless presentation systems. Whether any copied or bought Ubiq is not documented in the sources found.

market_need_then: The company's own site says conference room AV is hard to use without IT help. A July 2016 trade article describes a product aimed at meeting room productivity. A 2017 TechCrunch Demo Day writeup reported company-stated deployment at over 150 companies, which is unverified.

branding.domain_note: Used goubiq.com, not the exact ubiq.com. Dates not found.

identity.visual_style: plain product site with feature icons and customer testimonials

brand_strength.rationale: No press about the brand, mascot or community found. Many unrelated companies share the name Ubiq, which would make search harder.

outcome_analysis: Ubiq built a wireless presentation hub for meeting rooms in a category that Mersive and Barco already served. It raised a small seed, appears in YC S16 and reported early deployments, but the YC page lists it as inactive and no public post-mortem or shutdown cause was found. The cause of the inactive status is not public, so failure factors are left empty. The company site footer reads 2018, which suggests activity stopped around then.
notes: The seed round of 120K USD with Y Combinator and Bolt rests on a single database (CB Insights, with Company Check dating it to June 2016); another aggregator lists a smaller figure. Tracxn says Ubiq was acquired by British Engineering Services and names a different co-founder, which is unverified and conflicts with the YC page. Gust lists Waterloo and a 2014 founding date, CB Insights lists Boston. Barco ClickShare is a likely rival but no source dated near the batch was opened.
